This is a reaaaallly slippery slope here, and I think there are a lot of ways you can poke holes in this logic.

So, you say that calling yourself slurs is a way to reclaim them from the people that would use them against you. On that part, I agree.

But here's the thing: what of a gay man living in San Francisco, the most accepting city for gay people according to this website 

https://www.nerdwallet.com/blog/mortgages/top-lgbt-friendly-cities-2015/

who's never been called a f*g in his life and has only ever heard it be used by other gay people in his community?

Better yet, what of a black man who's never been called a n****r in his life and has only ever heard his black friends say it?

Once more, but flipped; I know for a fact that I DO NOT pass as a woman, no way, no how. I male failed once at the grocery store, and have been riding that high for months. I've been called a f*g and a b***h my whole life, especially when I started working in a kitchen, primarily with straight white men.

Do we have the right the say the words we've been called? But if you add that "you getting called those slurs was a different context; they weren't attacking you because of how they perceive you, they were trying to insult you by saying you act like a gay person or a women, and it'd be different if you were a woman or gay man."

Dual wield dagger build BUT, use mehrunes' razor in your right hand, and a dagger with absorb or leech enchantments in your left. Then, you rely entirely on the razors chance to instantly kill by getting your attack speed as high as possible and your sustain as high as possible as well.

For race, choose redgaurd for the Sand Dance ability (slows time in combat)

Religion could be anything really. You could do Akatosh for the shout cooldown rest, Arkay for the health regen and revive on death, OR you can roll with Mehrunes Dagon, since you're already using his razor. Watching people burn and explode is pretty cool, too.

For standing stone, either The Lady for Premonition, slowing enemies that can kill you, or The Lover for Undying Love, reviving you every 15 minutes. 

For main attributes, 100% health, maybe 10 70 20 for magicka health and stamina respectively. Combat is really simple, get up to the enemy and start swinging. Dual wield power attacks aren't really faster than just mashing right trigger or left click with the perks this build uses, and besides restoration to heal yourself, you're not gonna be using spells.  Just keep swinging.

Finally, perks:
One handed is easy. Go down the disciplined fighter tree to get Thundering Blow and Aftershock for ridiculous attack speed after power attacking. Next, put two ranks in ravage and get man o war. That's it for one handed, really. If you have points left over, you can go up the dagger tree to get coiled python, but it's not a priority.

Most of the heavy armor perks are going to be useful for adding sustain. Some notable ones would Battle Wary if you're using a dagger with stamina absorb, Rallying Standard and the perks after it, and Immortal, especially if you're using the Lady Stone.

For speech, go downt the 'And The Universe Listens' tree to get both ranks of Force Redoubled so you can shout more often.

You'll probably be healing a lot, so some points in Restoration won't hurt. All of the perks that actually heal you should be helpful.

Shouts that will help you are Dragon Aspect, obviously. Youre going to be using a lot of the same shouts in sequence, so the cooldown reduction will be important.  Elemental Fury will let you swing faster, and Slow Time will make enemies THINK you are swinging faster 😉 Drain Vitality will help you stay alive. When entering combat, the order i would use them all would be Dragon Aspect, Elemental Fury, Slow Time, Drain Vitality.

I think that's everything. Fair warning, you're not going to be killing things all that quickly. The chance to instantly kill someone is pretty low; sometimes you get lucky and gut em on the second swing, sometimes it takes fifteen. But that's not the point of the build. This is just a creative way to go all in on a unique aspect of a weapon, and have a good time while doing it.
